chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Yusuf al-Baghdadi al-Warraq narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Anbasa, the freedman of al-Rashid, narrated to us, saying: Darim ibn Qubaysa ibn Nahshal ibn Mujamma al-Sanaani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them both) narrated to us, saying: My father Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both), from the Prophet (may God bless him and his family), who said:

God, Mighty and Majestic, created one hundred thousand prophets and twenty-four thousand prophets — I am the noblest of them before God, and this is no boast. And God, Mighty and Majestic, created one hundred thousand deputies and twenty-four thousand deputies — Ali is the noblest of them before God and the most preferred of them.

Al-Shaykh [al-Saduq] said: And Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Baghdadi al-Warraq also narrated this hadith to me, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad, the freedman of al-Rashid, narrated to us, saying: Darim ibn Qubaysa narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), from the Prophet (may God bless him and his family).
ai.seo_question: How many prophets and deputies did God create according to the Prophet Muhammad through the Golden Chain narration?
ai.summary: A Prophetic tradition transmitted through the illustrious Golden Chain (Silsilat al-Dhahab) via Imam al-Rida, in which the Prophet Muhammad declares that God created 124,000 prophets — of whom he is the noblest — and 124,000 deputies (awsiya), of whom Ali ibn Abi Talib is the noblest and most preferred. Al-Saduq provides a second chain of transmission through Zayd ibn Ali for corroboration. This hadith establishes the concept of divinely appointed prophets and their successors as parallel institutions, affirming Ali's supreme rank among all deputies as a matter of divine decree rather than self-praise.
